Put $A=\mathbb Z[v,v^{-1}]$, $q=v^2$, $N\ge1$, $r\ge0$, $V=A^N$, and $T=V^{\otimes r}$. Let $U_{\mathbb Q(v)}(\mathfrak{gl}_N)$ have the presentation of [[def-hh-type-a-quantum-tensor-action-for-centralizers]] with its indeterminate renamed $v$ and its diagonal generators written $K_j$. Define $U_A$ to be its $A$-subalgebra generated by $K_j^{\pm1}$, $E_i^{(a)}=E_i^a/[a]_v!$, $F_i^{(a)}=F_i^a/[a]_v!$, and
$$\begin{bmatrix}K_j;0\\t\end{bmatrix}=\prod_{s=1}^t\frac{K_jv^{1-s}-K_j^{-1}v^{s-1}}{v^s-v^{-s}}\qquad(t\ge0).$$
Use $K_je_b=v^{\delta_{jb}}e_b$, $E_ie_b=\delta_{b,i+1}e_i$, $F_ie_b=\delta_{b,i}e_{i+1}$ and the coproduct
$$\Delta(E_i)=1\otimes E_i+E_i\otimes K_iK_{i+1}^{-1},\qquad\Delta(F_i)=K_i^{-1}K_{i+1}\otimes F_i+F_i\otimes1,\qquad\Delta(K_j)=K_j\otimes K_j.$$
The resulting action preserves $T$ and commutes with the right $H_{A,q}(S_r)$ action
$$e_{\ldots ab\ldots}T_s=\begin{cases}v e_{\ldots ba\ldots}&a<b,\\q e_{\ldots aa\ldots}&a=b,\\(q-1)e_{\ldots ab\ldots}+v e_{\ldots ba\ldots}&a>b.\end{cases}$$
It gives a surjection
$$\rho:U_A\longrightarrow\operatorname{End}_{H_{A,q}(S_r)}(T)\cong S_A(N,r)$$
onto the actual permutation-module endomorphism algebra of [[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]]. Its composition-weight projections are
$$1_\mu=\rho\left(\prod_{j=1}^N\begin{bmatrix}K_j;0\\\mu_j\end{bmatrix}\right)\qquad(\mu\in\Lambda(N,r)).$$
Every statement survives any homomorphism $A\to R$ to a commutative ring, including parameters at arbitrary roots of unity; $S_A\otimes_A R$ is the actual specialized endomorphism algebra. The proof supplies a terminating exact divided-power expression for each integral orbit-basis map, with Laurent-unit pivots.

Let $\tau$ be the antiautomorphism $E_i\leftrightarrow F_i$, $K_j\mapsto K_j$, let $*$ be the current cellular antiautomorphism of $S_A$, and put $C=\sum_\mu c_\mu1_\mu$, $c_\mu=v^{-\sum_j\binom{\mu_j}{2}}$. Then
$$\rho(\tau(u))=C^{-1}\rho(u)^*C\qquad(u\in U_A).$$

There is also a square-root-free version over $B=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. On the permutation-module word basis define weight-block operators $\mathcal E_{i,a,\mu}$ and $\mathcal F_{i,a,\mu}$, zero outside content $\mu$, by replacing a subset $J$ of $a$ occurrences of $i+1$ by $i$, or of $i$ by $i+1$, respectively, with coefficients
$$q^{\sum_{j\in J}\#i(w_{>j})},\qquad q^{\sum_{j\in J}\#(i+1)(w_{<j})}.$$
Together with $1_\mu$ these generate $S_B(N,r)$. After $q=v^2$ they are precisely $v^{a(\mu_{i+1}-a)}\rho(E_i^{(a)})1_\mu$ and $v^{a(\mu_i-a)}\rho(F_i^{(a)})1_\mu$. Thus this generating assertion holds over every original coefficient ring with any unit $q$, whether or not $q$ has a square root. This assertion concerns the displayed polynomial action algebra; it does not assert a quantum group presentation over the original ring without choosing $v$.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^{	imes}$, $d,n\ge0$, and $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$ ([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). Let $\Lambda(d,n)$ be the set of weak compositions $\mu=(\mu_1,\dots,\mu_d)$ of $n$ (so $\mu_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ and $\sum_i\mu_i=n$; zero parts are allowed and give empty rows). For $\mu\in\Lambda(d,n)$ let $m_\mu=\sum_{w\in S_\mu}T_w$ ([[def-murphy-elements-and-murphy-tableau-elements]]) and let $M^{\mu}:=m_\mu H$ be the right ideal it generates, the **(Hecke) permutation module**; $M^{\mu}$ is free over $R$ with basis $\{m_\mu T_{d(t)}:t	ext{ row-standard }\mu	ext{-tableau}\}$ and is the Hecke analogue of the module induced from the trivial representation of the Young subgroup ([[def-young-subgroup-tabloid-and-permutation-module]]).

For a weak composition $\mu\in\Lambda(d,n)$, define $T_0(\lambda,\mu)$ to be the fillings of $[\lambda]$ by $1,\ldots,d$ with exactly $\mu_i$ entries equal to $i$, weakly increasing rows and strictly increasing columns. Put $T_0(\lambda)= igcup_{\mu\in\Lambda(d,n)}T_0(\lambda,\mu)$ and $K_{\lambda\mu}:=|T_0(\lambda,\mu)|$. This explicitly extends the partition-content definition of [[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]] to weak compositions, including internal zero counts; a zero count means that its label is absent. The set is finite, since at most $d^n$ fillings occur for $n>0$, and at $n=0$ its unique member is the empty filling.

Here is the freeness statement in detail: the cosets $S_\mu d$ with $d\in D_\mu$ partition $S_n$, and $\ell(ud)=\ell(u)+\ell(d)$ for $u\in S_\mu$, $d\in D_\mu$ ([[def-murphy-elements-and-murphy-tableau-elements]]), so the standard basis theorem ([[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]) gives $T_uT_{d(t)}=T_{ud(t)}$ and $m_\mu T_{d(t)}=\sum_{u\in S_\mu}T_{u\,d(t)}$; these are the standard basis elements indexed by the single coset $S_\mu d(t)$, and the cosets are disjoint, whence $M^\mu= igoplus_tR\,m_\mu T_{d(t)}$ is free with the displayed basis as $t$ runs over the row-standard $\mu$-tableaux.

For every dominant label weight $\lambda$, let $V_A=U_Av_\lambda=U_A^-v_\lambda$ be the integral highest lattice inside the simple integrable module $L(\lambda)$, over $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. Then each label-weight component of $V_A$ is finite free of rank $\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}L(\lambda)_\mu$, not merely torsionfree, and $V_A$ spans the field module. For every characteristic-zero field $k$ specialized at $q=1$, the fibre has the same weight dimensions and is the classical simple integrable highest weight module of the explicitly regularized realization, transported back to the original label lattice; hence its character is the Weyl–Kac character, the finite Weyl character in finite type. The integral quotient $U_A^-/\sum_i\sum_{s>\lambda(h_i)}U_A^-F_i^{(s)}$ is $V_A(\lambda)$; its field extension is $L(\lambda)$ in every symmetrizable type.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $V=\mathbb C^r$, $r\ge1$
([[def-schur-module-and-schur-polynomial-character]]), and let $\lambda$ be a
partition with $\ell(\lambda)\le r$
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]). Then
$$\operatorname{ch}S_\lambda(V)=\sum_T x^{\operatorname{wt}(T)},$$
the sum over all semistandard tableaux $T$ of shape $\lambda$ with entries in
$\{1,\dots,r\}$, where $\operatorname{wt}(T)=(a_1,\dots,a_r)$ records the
multiplicity of each entry
([[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]],
[[def-skew-diagram-and-semistandard-skew-tableau]]). Moreover this polynomial
is the rank-$r$ Schur polynomial $s_\lambda(x_1,\dots,x_r)$ of
[[def-stable-schur-function-by-bialternants]], i.e.
$$s_\lambda(x_1,\dots,x_r)=\frac{a_{\lambda+\delta_r}(x_1,\dots,x_r)}{a_{\delta_r}(x_1,\dots,x_r)}=\sum_Tx^{\operatorname{wt}(T)}$$
for $\ell(\lambda)\le r$, while $s_\lambda(x_1,\dots,x_r):=0$ and
$\operatorname{ch}S_\lambda(V)=0$ when $\ell(\lambda)>r$. In particular
$S_\lambda(V)\ne0$ if and only if $\ell(\lambda)\le r$, and the multiplicity of
the weight $\alpha$ in $S_\lambda(V)$ equals the number of semistandard
tableaux of shape $\lambda$ and weight $\alpha$; by
[[lem-bender-knuth-involutions-on-semistandard-tableaux]] this polynomial is
symmetric in $x_1,\dots,x_r$.

Fix $r\ge1$ and a skew shape $\nu/\lambda$ (for a partition shape take
$\lambda=\varnothing$), let $k\in\{1,\dots,r-1\}$, and let $T$ be a
semistandard skew tableau of shape $\nu/\lambda$ with entries in
$\{1,\dots,r\}$ ([[def-skew-diagram-and-semistandard-skew-tableau]],
[[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]]). Call an entry $k$ or $k+1$ of
$T$ **free** if there is no $k+1$ respectively no $k$ in the same column. Then:

(i) the free positions in each row occupy consecutive cells of that row;
(ii) replacing in every row the free $k$'s and free $k+1$'s by their
complementary counts (if the row has $a_i$ free $k$'s and $b_i$ free $k+1$'s,
then after the replacement it has $b_i$ free $k$'s and $a_i$ free $k+1$'s in
the same free cells, the remaining entries unchanged, the free cells filled
from left to right by the $b_i$ copies of $k$ followed by the $a_i$ copies of
$k+1$) produces again a semistandard skew tableau $\sigma_k(T)$ of the same
shape, with entries in $\{1,\dots,r\}$;
(iii) $\sigma_k$ is an involution of the set of semistandard skew tableaux of
shape $\nu/\lambda$ with the same set of free positions, and
$\operatorname{wt}(\sigma_k(T))=s_k\operatorname{wt}(T)$, where $s_k$ is the
transposition of $k$ and $k+1$ acting on weights
([[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]], with weights read as vectors
in $\mathbb Z^r$).

Consequently, for every weight $\alpha\in\mathbb Z^r_{\ge0}$ the number of
semistandard skew tableaux of shape $\nu/\lambda$ and weight $\alpha$ equals
the number of weight $s_k\alpha$, and the generating function
$\sum_Tx^{\operatorname{wt}(T)}$, over semistandard skew tableaux of shape
$\nu/\lambda$ with entries in $\{1,\dots,r\}$, is symmetric in
$x_1,\dots,x_r$ ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]).

Let $i\in I$ and let $T_{i,c,t}$ be the toral quantum binomials of
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]
($i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$, $t\ge0$, $T_{i,c,0}=1$), inside the Drinfeld–Jimbo
algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]
with $U_A$ and its parts $U_A^-,U_A^0,U_A^+$ as in that definition. Write
$E=E_i$, $F=F_i$, $E^{(a)}=E_i^{(a)}$, $F^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}$ for the divided
powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] and put
$q=q_i$ inside the displayed formulas.

(i) **Divided-power multiplication.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E^{(a)}E^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iE^{(a+b)},\qquad F^{(a)}F^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iF^{(a+b)}.$$

(ii) **Toral recursion and commutation.** For $t\ge1$,
$$T_{i,c,t}=\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-t+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+t-1}}{q_i^{\,t}-q_i^{\,-t}}\,T_{i,c,t-1}.$$
Each $T_{i,c,t}$ is a Laurent polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in
$\mathbb Q(q)$; the toral elements commute with one another and with all $K_h$.
For all $i,j$ and all $m\in\mathbb Z$ one has
$K_i^{\,m}T_{j,c,t}=T_{j,c,t}K_i^{\,m}$ if $i\ne j$, while
$E_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-2,t}E_i$, $E_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-a_{ij},t}E_j$,
$F_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+2,t}F_i$, $F_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+a_{ij},t}F_j$ for all $j$.
In particular $E_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0E_i$, $F_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0F_i$,
$T_{i,c,t}E_i=E_iT_{i,c+2,t}\in E_iU_A^0$ and
$T_{i,c,t}F_i=F_iT_{i,c-2,t}\in F_iU_A^0$: the toral factor can be moved to the
middle at the cost of a shift of the binomial index.

(iii) **Reordering identity.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}=\sum_{t=0}^{\min(a,b)}F_i^{(b-t)}\,T_{i,\,2t-a-b,\,t}\,E_i^{(a-t)},$$
with every coefficient a toral quantum binomial in $U_A^0$. In particular
$E_iF_i-F_iE_i=T_{i,0,1}$ and
$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(a)}=\sum_{t=0}^{a}F_i^{(a-t)}T_{i,2t-2a,t}E_i^{(a-t)}$.
For $i\ne j$, $E_i^{(a)}$ and $F_j^{(b)}$ commute; the same-half divided powers
$E_i^{(a)},E_j^{(b)}$ (and likewise $F_i^{(a)},F_j^{(b)}$) commute whenever
$a_{ij}=0$, and for $a_{ij}\ne0$ no commutation is asserted.

(iv) **Triangular spanning.** Every element of $U_A$ is an $A$-linear
combination of products $b_-u\,b_+$ with $b_-\in U_A^-$, $u\in U_A^0$ and
$b_+\in U_A^+$; equivalently $U_A=U_A^-U_A^0U_A^+$ as an $A$-module. No
independence of the spanning family is asserted.

Put $A=\mathbb Z[v,v^{-1}]$, and use the integral $U_A(\mathfrak{gl}_N)$ of [[lem-integral-divided-power-tensor-action-surjects-onto-type-a-q-schur-algebra]]. Let $R$ be any commutative $A$-algebra and $U_R=R\otimes_AU_A$. Let $X$ be a left $U_R$-module with a specified composition-label decomposition
$$X=\bigoplus_{\mu\in\Lambda(N,r)}X_\mu,$$
where $r\ge0$, $\Lambda(N,r)$ consists of nonnegative integer $N$-tuples of total $r$, every integral toral element acts on $X_\mu$ by its integer-weight character $\mu$, and the positive and negative divided powers shift labels by their root degrees. Thus the toral rank-one binomial with indices $c,t$ acts by $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}\mu_i-\mu_{i+1}+c\\t\end{smallmatrix}\right]_v$. This requirement uses the full integral toral characters, including specialized binomials; it does not recover labels from the specialized $K_j$ eigenvalues. Each $X_\mu$ may be an arbitrary $R$-module.

For a partition $\lambda\in\Lambda(N,r)$ and a vector $x\in X_\lambda$ killed by every $E_i^{(s)}$, $s>0$, put $m_i=\lambda_i-\lambda_{i+1}$. Then
$$F_i^{(a)}x=0\qquad(1\le i<N,\ a>m_i).$$
These are all divided powers beyond the highest bound, including those whose quantum factorial vanishes after specialization. Consequently, if $X=U_Rx$, the highest-vector map gives a surjection of negative-half modules
$$U_R^-/\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\sum_{a>m_i}U_R^-F_i^{(a)}\longrightarrow X,\qquad 1\longmapsto x.$$
Whenever this quotient carries its integral highest-module action, with the same toral character and positive annihilation on $1$, that map is a $U_R$-module map. In particular it applies to the actual highest quotient used by the normalized q-Schur Weyl-cell comparison. No Schur factorization of $X$ is assumed. The relation proof and negative-half surjection are choice-free and hold at every specialization, over rings with torsion and zero divisors as well as fields.

derivations.claim: Tableau support. In any semistandard tableau, each column has at most $k$ entries in $\{1,\ldots,k\}$; summing over columns gives $\sum_{j\le k}\mu_j\le\sum_{j\le k}\lambda_j$. By [F4] the same inequality holds after permuting the content. Thus no weight $\lambda+a\alpha_i$, $a>0$, occurs. No weight $\lambda-a\alpha_i$ occurs when $a>m_i$: swapping its $i$th and $(i+1)$st coordinates makes its first $i$ coordinates sum to $\sum_{j\le i}\lambda_j+a-m_i$, violating that inequality. Negative coordinates also cannot occur. The type-$\lambda$ tableau is uniquely $T^\lambda$: the first content inequality is an equality forcing all $1$'s into row one, and successively equality for $k$ forces all $k$'s into row $k$. Hence the top weight line is $Ah$.

The highest map. The action in the Statement is a left action since $\tau$ reverses products. It has the stated weight labels by [F1]. Step 1.1 kills every $E_i^{(a)}h$ for $a>0$ and every $F_i^{(a)}h$ for $a>m_i$; the toral characters are those of weight $\lambda$. Thus [F3] gives a highest-module map $f:Q_A(\lambda)\to W_A^\lambda$. By the cell product and $B_{\rm cell}(h,h)=1$, $h\varphi_{T^\lambda T}=w_T$. Surjectivity in [F1] supplies an integral preimage under $\rho\tau$ of each of these endomorphisms, so $h$ generates the whole cell and $f$ is onto.

Cellular highest induction over any $R$. Put $I^{>\lambda}$ equal to the span of cellular shapes strictly dominating $\lambda$. This ideal is generated by the $1_\eta$ for $\eta>\lambda$: choose a finite order with larger shapes first, and use $\varphi_{S,T^\eta}1_\eta\varphi_{T^\eta,T}\equiv\varphi_{ST}$ modulo higher shapes, whose coefficient is $1$ by [F2]. Induction absorbs those higher terms in the already generated ideal; conversely each $1_\eta$ lies in $I^{>\lambda}$. The quotient $S_R1_\lambda/I^{>\lambda}1_\lambda$ has exactly the basis $\varphi_{T,T^\lambda}$ of shape $\lambda$: any semistandard type $\lambda$ in shape $\eta$ forces $\eta\unrhd\lambda$ by the column count in step 1.1, and shape $\lambda$ has the single second tableau $T^\lambda$. Star identifies this left cell with the right cell acted on by $s^*$; the weight-unit map sending its weight-$\mu$ basis vector to $(c_\mu/c_\lambda)w_T$ instead identifies it with the action $s\cdot w=wC^{-1}s^*C$ of the Statement. Its highest vector maps to $h$.

Integral isomorphism. In type $A_{N-1}$ the finite Weyl alternating quotient of [F3], on composition labels of fixed total $r$, is $\det(x_i^{\lambda_j+N-j})/\det(x_i^{N-j})$: the Weyl group permutes the $N$ coordinates, and multiplying numerator and denominator by the common monomial removes the half-sum shifts. This is the bialternant of [F4]. Consequently, for each weight $\mu$, [F3] and [F4] make the source and target finite free of the same rank $K_{\lambda\mu}$. The map in step 2.1 is graded, hence onto on each weight. Choose finite free bases and write its square matrix $D$; lifting the finitely many target basis vectors gives a matrix $P$ with $DP=I$. Therefore $\det(D)\det(P)=1$, and the adjugate formula gives an inverse matrix over $A$. Zero-rank weights have the unique empty inverse. Only finitely many weights occur, so these inverses assemble to $f^{-1}$. This proves the entire quotient presentation and the basis $b_T$. Concretely a preimage under the surjection of $\varphi_{T^\lambda T}$, followed by integral triangular spanning and highest-character evaluation, gives a representative of $b_T$ in $U_A^-$; different preimages give the same quotient class. No generic-rank argument replaces the proved integral surjection.

Let $X=U_Rx$ be the cyclic highest module with the composition support and full toral characters in the Statement. By [F6], every divided highest relation holds, and the highest-vector map $Q_R(\lambda)\to X$ is a surjective $U_R$-module map. The integral isomorphism of step 3.1 and its inverse remain inverses after arbitrary base change. Thus this is a quotient of the actual normalized Weyl cell. In particular $X$ factors through $S_R$: [F1] makes $\ker\rho$ stable under $\tau$, so it annihilates that cell and every quotient. No factorization of $X$ was assumed. Via the unit identification of step 2.2, the corresponding left-cell quotient map preserves the highest generator. Apply this argument also to $Y=S_R\otimes_{S_R^+}R_\lambda$: its canonical generator has the stated toral character, is killed by all positive divided powers, and is fixed by $1_\lambda$. The last assertion follows because the integral toral projection $\prod_j\left[\begin{smallmatrix}K_j;0\\\lambda_j\end{smallmatrix}\right]$ is $1_\lambda$ and has highest-character value $1$. Thus $Y$ is a quotient of the left cell. Conversely the highest vector of that cell defines a surjection $Y$ onto it. Both compositions fix the cyclic highest generators, hence are identities, proving the induction equivalence. This is a direct cellular proof of the universal property.

Construct the form on the actual cell first. Give weight $\mu$ the scalar $d_\mu=c_\lambda/c_\mu$ times $B_{m cell}$ and pair distinct weights by zero. Weight spaces are orthogonal for $B_{m cell}$ because its self-adjoint projections $1_\mu$ are orthogonal; thus the new form is symmetric and integral and has value $1$ on $h$. For $s=ho(u)$, [F1] gives $ho(	au(u))^*=CsC^{-1}$. On a homogeneous component, right multiplication by this conjugate contributes $c_
u/c_\mu$ when $s$ takes right weight $
u$ to right weight $\mu$. Hence $d_
u(c_
u/c_\mu)=d_\mu$, and cellular contravariance gives $B(u\cdot a,b)=B(a,	au(u)\cdot b)$. Linearity handles sums of homogeneous components. Pull this form back by the integral isomorphism $f$.

Highest coefficient and uniqueness. For $x,y\in U_A^-$, contravariance gives $B(xz,yz)=B(z,\tau(x)yz)$. Orthogonality and the top line $Az$ make the last expression exactly $[z](\tau(x)yz)$. This proves the displayed coefficient construction descends through the complete quotient, including both arguments, because the already constructed form is defined on that quotient. Conversely the same equality is forced for any homogeneous normalized contravariant form, and negative words span by [F3], proving uniqueness. The construction has used only Laurent units and the integral action; it has not restricted a tensor form or divided by a tensor highest norm.

Base change and singular forms. Tensor the proved isomorphism and its inverse with any $R$; the quotient is its specialized presentation by right exactness of tensor product, the basis remains the specialized $b_T$, and the integral form matrices and highest projection specialize entrywise. The weight factors $d_\mu$ remain units. Thus a vector pairs to zero for the specialized form exactly when its image pairs to zero for the specialized cellular form, even if the Gram determinant is zero. Steps 2.2 and 4.1 used the same free cellular basis and unit coefficients over $R$, so their universal property also holds without flatness. At $r=0$ the unique empty highest cell and quotient are $R$ with form $1$; at $N=1$ the only degree-$r$ cell and quotient are likewise rank one. These prove all claims with only the inherited Choice of [C1].

Let $U_{\mathbb Q(v)}(\mathfrak{gl}_N)$ have the presentation of [[def-hh-type-a-quantum-tensor-action-for-centralizers]] with its indeterminate renamed $v$ and its diagonal generators written $K_j$. Define $U_A$ to be its $A$-subalgebra generated by $K_j^{\pm1}$, $E_i^{(a)}=E_i^a/[a]_v!$, $F_i^{(a)}=F_i^a/[a]_v!$, and

Use $K_je_b=v^{\delta_{jb}}e_b$, $E_ie_b=\delta_{b,i+1}e_i$, $F_ie_b=\delta_{b,i}e_{i+1}$ and the coproduct
$$\Delta(E_i)=1\otimes E_i+E_i\otimes K_iK_{i+1}^{-1},\qquad\Delta(F_i)=K_i^{-1}K_{i+1}\otimes F_i+F_i\otimes1,\qquad\Delta(K_j)=K_j\otimes K_j.$$
The resulting action preserves $T$ and commutes with the right $H_{A,q}(S_r)$ action

It gives a surjection

onto the actual permutation-module endomorphism algebra of [[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]]. Its composition-weight projections are
$$1_\mu=\rho\left(\prod_{j=1}^N\begin{bmatrix}K_j;0\\\mu_j\end{bmatrix}\right)\qquad(\mu\in\Lambda(N,r)).$$
Every statement survives any homomorphism $A\to R$ to a commutative ring, including parameters at arbitrary roots of unity; $S_A\otimes_A R$ is the actual specialized endomorphism algebra. There is also a square-root-free version over $B=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. On the permutation-module word basis define weight-block operators $\mathcal E_{i,a,\mu}$ and $\mathcal F_{i,a,\mu}$, zero outside content $\mu$, by replacing a subset $J$ of $a$ occurrences of $i+1$ by $i$, or of $i$ by $i+1$, respectively, with coefficients

This assertion concerns the displayed polynomial action algebra; it does not assert a quantum group presentation over the original ring without choosing $v$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited only through the integral highest-lattice supplier. Put $A=\mathbb Z[v,v^{-1}]$, $q=v^2$, $N\ge1$, and $r\ge0$. Fix $r\ge1$ and a skew shape $\nu/\lambda$ (for a partition shape take
$\lambda=\varnothing$), let $k\in\{1,\dots,r-1\}$, and let $T$ be a
semistandard skew tableau of shape $\nu/\lambda$ with entries in
$\{1,\dots,r\}$ ([[def-skew-diagram-and-semistandard-skew-tableau]],
[[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]]). Call an entry $k$ or $k+1$ of
$T$ **free** if there is no $k+1$ respectively no $k$ in the same column. Then:

(i) the free positions in each row occupy consecutive cells of that row;
(ii) replacing in every row the free $k$'s and free $k+1$'s by their
complementary counts (if the row has $a_i$ free $k$'s and $b_i$ free $k+1$'s,
then after the replacement it has $b_i$ free $k$'s and $a_i$ free $k+1$'s in
the same free cells, the remaining entries unchanged, the free cells filled
from left to right by the $b_i$ copies of $k$ followed by the $a_i$ copies of
$k+1$) produces again a semistandard skew tableau $\sigma_k(T)$ of the same
shape, with entries in $\{1,\dots,r\}$;
(iii) $\sigma_k$ is an involution of the set of semistandard skew tableaux of
shape $\nu/\lambda$ with the same set of free positions, and
$\operatorname{wt}(\sigma_k(T))=s_k\operatorname{wt}(T)$, where $s_k$ is the
transposition of $k$ and $k+1$ acting on weights
([[def-semistandard-tableau-and-kostka-number]], with weights read as vectors

Consequently, for every weight $\alpha\in\mathbb Z^r_{\ge0}$ the number of
semistandard skew tableaux of shape $\nu/\lambda$ and weight $\alpha$ equals
the number of weight $s_k\alpha$, and the generating function
$\sum_Tx^{\operatorname{wt}(T)}$, over semistandard skew tableaux of shape
$\nu/\lambda$ with entries in $\{1,\dots,r\}$, is symmetric in

Let $i\in I$ and let $T_{i,c,t}$ be the toral quantum binomials of

($i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$, $t\ge0$, $T_{i,c,0}=1$), inside the Drinfeld–Jimbo
algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]
with $U_A$ and its parts $U_A^-,U_A^0,U_A^+$ as in that definition. Write
$E=E_i$, $F=F_i$, $E^{(a)}=E_i^{(a)}$, $F^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}$ for the divided
powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] and put
$q=q_i$ inside the displayed formulas.

(i) **Divided-power multiplication.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E^{(a)}E^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iE^{(a+b)},\qquad F^{(a)}F^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iF^{(a+b)}.$$

(ii) **Toral recursion and commutation.** For $t\ge1$,
$$T_{i,c,t}=\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-t+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+t-1}}{q_i^{\,t}-q_i^{\,-t}}\,T_{i,c,t-1}.$$
Each $T_{i,c,t}$ is a Laurent polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in
$\mathbb Q(q)$; the toral elements commute with one another and with all $K_h$.
For all $i,j$ and all $m\in\mathbb Z$ one has
$K_i^{\,m}T_{j,c,t}=T_{j,c,t}K_i^{\,m}$ if $i\ne j$, while
$E_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-2,t}E_i$, $E_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-a_{ij},t}E_j$,
$F_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+2,t}F_i$, $F_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+a_{ij},t}F_j$ for all $j$.
In particular $E_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0E_i$, $F_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0F_i$,
$T_{i,c,t}E_i=E_iT_{i,c+2,t}\in E_iU_A^0$ and
$T_{i,c,t}F_i=F_iT_{i,c-2,t}\in F_iU_A^0$: the toral factor can be moved to the
middle at the cost of a shift of the binomial index.

(iii) **Reordering identity.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}=\sum_{t=0}^{\min(a,b)}F_i^{(b-t)}\,T_{i,\,2t-a-b,\,t}\,E_i^{(a-t)},$$
with every coefficient a toral quantum binomial in $U_A^0$. In particular
$E_iF_i-F_iE_i=T_{i,0,1}$ and
$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(a)}=\sum_{t=0}^{a}F_i^{(a-t)}T_{i,2t-2a,t}E_i^{(a-t)}$.
For $i\ne j$, $E_i^{(a)}$ and $F_j^{(b)}$ commute; the same-half divided powers
$E_i^{(a)},E_j^{(b)}$ (and likewise $F_i^{(a)},F_j^{(b)}$) commute whenever
$a_{ij}=0$, and for $a_{ij}\ne0$ no commutation is asserted.

(iv) **Triangular spanning.** Every element of $U_A$ is an $A$-linear
combination of products $b_-u\,b_+$ with $b_-\in U_A^-$, $u\in U_A^0$ and
$b_+\in U_A^+$; equivalently $U_A=U_A^-U_A^0U_A^+$ as an $A$-module. No
independence of the spanning family is asserted.

u/c_\mu$ is canceled by $(c_\lambda/c_
u)(c_

Construct the corner over the original $R,q$. Put $M_0=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Lambda(N-1,d-1)}m_\alpha H_{d-1}$. Length-additive parabolic coset bases identify $M_1=\bigoplus_\alpha m_{(\alpha,1)}H_d$ with $M_0\otimes_{H_{d-1}}H_d$, by $m_\alpha h\otimes a\mapsto m_\alpha ha$. Hence $f\mapsto f\otimes1$, extended by zero on the other summands, embeds the lower Schur algebra with identity $p=\sum_{\alpha_N=1}1_\alpha$. It is injective because the unit parabolic coset supplies a direct summand. The lower regular composition induces the upper regular type $\omega_*=(1^{d-1},0^{N-d},1)$, so $e_{\rm lower}pV=e_*V$. On that summand the lower Hecke corner acts by left multiplication by exactly $h\in H_{d-1}$ on $H_d$, since $h\otimes a\mapsto ha$.

Use the root convention $F_{i,i+1}=F_i$ and $F_{i,j}=vF_{i+1,j}F_i-F_iF_{i+1,j}$. In the negative algebra, its last-simple-root-degree-one part is spanned by $xF_{i,N}$ with $x$ in the negative lower Levi. Here is a direct spanning proof, requiring no specialized PBW independence. Every divided-simple-generator word of this degree has exactly one $F_{N-1}$, exponent one; all other generators belong to the lower Levi. Move each factor to its right past the current root using $$F_{i,N}F_{i-1}^{(s)}=v^{-s}F_{i-1}^{(s)}F_{i,N}+v^{-1}F_{i-1}^{(s-1)}F_{i-1,N},\qquad F_{i,N}F_i^{(s)}=v^sF_i^{(s)}F_{i,N}.$$ Other lower simple divided generators commute with $F_{i,N}$. The first identity follows from $vF_{i,N}F_{i-1}=F_{i-1}F_{i,N}+F_{i-1,N}$ and $F_{i-1,N}F_{i-1}=vF_{i-1}F_{i-1,N}$: induction on ordinary powers gives coefficient $v^{-1}[s]$, canceled with $[s]!$ in the generic algebra, leaving the displayed integral identity. The second and remaining commutations follow by inserting the root recurrence into the rank-two Serre identity and then inducting on the interval length; the only noncommuting lower adjacent endpoint is $i-1$, already treated. Each move removes one right factor, so it terminates. Triangular spanning and the highest-vector relations now show $W^1=\sum_iU^-_{N-1}F_{i,N}z_\lambda$. If $\lambda_i=\lambda_{i+1}$, the weight $\lambda-\epsilon_i+\epsilon_{i+1}$ is absent: its sorted weight strictly dominates $\lambda$, contrary to the tableau support. Thus $F_i z_\lambda=0$ and the root recurrence gives $F_{i,N}z_\lambda=-F_iF_{i+1,N}z_\lambda$. Iteration removes all nonremovable rows. Rows beyond the height contribute zero by nonnegative weight support. Therefore the claimed removable-row generators span integrally.

Order these rows as $i_1>\cdots>i_t$, so $\mu_j=\lambda(i_j)$ decreases in dominance, and let $W_j$ be the negative lower-Levi span of the first $j$ generators, with $W_0=0$. Inductively suppose $W_{j-1}$ is invariant. In $W^1/W_{j-1}$ every weight lies below a remaining generator weight by step 2.1, and $\mu_j$ is their maximum. Every positive divided generator kills the image of $F_{i_j,N}z_\lambda$, since its target weight is strictly above $\mu_j$. Triangular spanning makes its negative span invariant. The actual universal highest property gives a surjection $W_{N-1}(\mu_j)\to W_j/W_{j-1}$. This proves invariance and these integral surjections at each stage, without dividing a quantum integer.

Exactly one entry $N$ in a semistandard $\lambda$-tableau lies at a removable corner, and deleting it gives a semistandard $\lambda(i)$-tableau on $1,\ldots,N-1$. Conversely appending $N$ at that corner preserves semistandardness. Consequently the actual free ranks satisfy $\operatorname{rank}W^1=\sum_j\operatorname{rank}W_{N-1}(\mu_j)$. Over $\mathbb Q(v)$ the surjections of step 3.1 and this dimension equality force equality of every quotient dimension. The kernel of each integral surjection lies in the free $A$-module $W_{N-1}(\mu_j)$ and has generic rank zero; injectivity into its fraction-field extension therefore makes that kernel zero. Each integral quotient is thus the actual free lower Weyl module. Its freeness makes the successive short exact sequences split as $A$-module sequences, so arbitrary base change preserves the filtration injections, quotients and surjections. Generic dimensions were used only to prove kernels of explicit integral surjections vanish, not to replace a specialized construction.

Over a field let $B^-$ denote the actual lower Borel image. A $B^-$-map $W^1\to F_\mu$ is determined by its values at the generators of step 2.1; their weights are distinct, so its dimension is at most one and is zero off $\mu_j$. At $\mu_j$, quotient by $W_{j-1}$. This quotient has no weight above $\mu_j$, its $\mu_j$-space is the one-dimensional generator line by step 4.1, and later generator weights lie strictly below it. Taking that generator's coefficient, and zero on every other weight, is a well-defined nonzero $B^-$-map, since a nonconstant negative operator cannot reach $\mu_j$. This proves dimension exactly one. The universal highest property gives $\operatorname{Hom}(W_{N-1}(\mu),X)=\operatorname{Hom}_{B^+}(F_\mu,X)$ for every polynomial $X$: maps are exactly primitive vectors of that weight. Taking contravariant duals identifies this with $\operatorname{Hom}_{B^-}(X^\tau,F_\mu)$. With $X=(W^1)^\tau$ this proves the first Hom assertion.
